description: Add tasks to the calendar, each in the plan's task contract (key, title, kind, channel, brief, reason, date, goalKey, dependsOn, engine, executor, verification, expected, cost), dated on a day of the horizon (situation.horizon). A task under an open slot's key (situation.slotsDue, situation.calendar.slots) firms that slot: it becomes the slot's full task. Up to 2 new tasks a run beside the slots it firms. Work Marsell makes (executor marsell) is one of these kinds on its engine: board on content, video on content, image on content, article on content, comparison on content, gbp_post on content, script on content, audit on content, prospect_list on content, concept on content, carousel on content, landing_section on content, repo_page on content, launch_kit on content, release_notes on content, list_entry on content, share_kit on content, day_kit on content, original on content, cut_list on content, post on social, reply_drafts on community, pitch on community, reply_inbox on community, reddit_post on community, answer_audit on search, ad_test on paid, create on convert, sequence on convert, site on sites, landing on sites. A job for the owner's own AI is kind homework on engine homework with executor agent, its brief the whole job, and only while their AI can take homework. Anything else is a two-minute owner action (kind fix or connect, executor owner_2min). They are checked against the playbook, the connections and each seven-day window: the tasks that pass are written, and the ones refused come back with why, to send again alone, fixed. Returns the new work ids, the slots firmed, the keys already on the calendar (the same piece, never a second one) and the tasks refused. A later day is a slot instead (slot_add); a running series of the same work is a stream (stream_set). It needs an act key.

project.description: The project's id or exact name. Optional when the account has one project.

rationale.description: Why these tasks now, in plain words; the owner reads it.

tasks.description: One or more tasks in the plan's task contract, each fully filled in.

brief.description: Written to whoever makes the piece: its job (what it is for, and what the person who meets it should do or feel), who it is for, its specific subject, and its ask or that it asks for nothing. It describes the piece and never writes it.

buildsOn.description: For a post (kind post) drawn from finished work already on file: the ids in input.researchOnFile it builds on, so it may state what their verified notes support. Empty for every other task. A task of this same plan is named in dependsOn instead.

cents.description: Estimated USD cents, not dollars or tokens. 100 Marsell tokens = 1 cent. Only use 0 for a known no-charge task; an unquoted cost is null on the task.

cost.description: A supported estimate in USD cents, or null when unknown/unquoted or the stage disallows spend. Null does not mean free; this field does not authorize spending.

date.description: The calendar day the piece is ready, YYYY-MM-DD: a day of input.horizon.week (today to its seventh day). Later days hold slots.

label.description: The piece itself in two to five words, as the owner would name it on a card: 'Sky Window Hoodie page', 'Fall looks with the Transit set', 'Frutiger Aero carousel', 'Restock Friday post'. No kind prefix with a colon, no brackets; the title and brief carry the rest.

pictures.description: For a task of kind image: how many pictures it makes when the owner asked for a number of them ('one picture' is 1, 'two pictures' is 2); null when they did not say, so Marsell's usual set size stands. Null for every other kind.

becomes.description: The whole part after the change, written out in full. When now is null: only the exact words to add, or the piece to replace and where it goes; or, when the owner asked for it, the whole new name or bio as they asked.

channel.description: The platform, as input.profiles names it (instagram, facebook, linkedin, tiktok, youtube…).

handle.description: The account's handle as input.profiles names it, without @; null when the account is not connected.

now.description: The whole part exactly as input.profiles gives it when its state is read, character for character with its punctuation, line breaks and emoji; "" when it was read empty; null when its state is anything else, for pinned posts, and when the account is not connected.

ownerAsked.description: True only when input.ownerAsks or a rule in input.memory asks for this new name or bio in the owner's own words.

part.description: Which part of the profile changes: name is the display name, never the @handle.

until.description: When becomes adds a line that holds a date (a drop, an event, a deadline): its last day, YYYY-MM-DD; the plan then holds the task or slot that takes it out within the week after. Null otherwise.

why.description: Why, in one or two plain sentences: what the change does for the business, what is cut to fit the limit, and why any line of its own that goes should go.

profileChange.description: For a task that changes the name, bio, link or pinned items of one of the business's own profiles: each part it changes, with its text now (from input.profiles) and its new text. Null for every other task.

reason.description: The line the owner reads under this task's title. In one short plain sentence said to them as 'you' (never 'the owner'), what it is for: the offer, people, goal or date it serves, or what it makes possible. Never Marsell's own workings or how the task came to be planned (a playbook, a weekly count or minimum, an 'Ask N' label, a retry, a free day, an engine), never the title again, and no 'today' or 'this week': it may be read days later.

series.description: The id of the series in input.series this task is an episode of: set it on an original Short whose channel is one of the channels of a series with weekShortsAreEpisodes. Null for every other task.

metric.description: An available observed metric. Draft delivery uses content_ready, not clips_live, signups, reach or sales.

rule.description: Evidence that would verify this task; keep artifact completion separate from later customer outcomes.
